land.text: Egypt as Cliopatria draws it for Muhammad Ali from 1811: the Nile valley, the Delta, Sinai and the Red Sea coast

predecessors.note: Egypt Eyalet. The Mamluk beys who held Upper Egypt (page: the Mamluks had extended rule 'south along the Nile River to Upper Egypt') have no dossier; see notes. Cliopatria keeps Egypt inside its Ottoman shape to 1810.

land.text: Egypt and the Sudan under the khedives

successors.note: The same state under a new title: a firman of 1866 and the khedive title of 1867 (Muhammad Ali dynasty history page); Cliopatria ends this row in 1865 and starts the Khedivate in 1866, so the dossier ends in 1865 to leave no overlap.

capitals.name: Cairo
capitals.note: The page refers to Cairo as 'the capital' in 1815; page silent on 1805.

rulers.name: Muhammad Ali Pasha
rulers.title: wali (governor) of Egypt
rulers.note: Infobox term from 17 May 1805; 'ruled until 1848, when senility made further governance by him impossible'; died 2 August 1849.

rulers.name: Ibrahim Pasha
rulers.note: Succeeded in September 1848, died in November 1848 (History of Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty).

rulers.name: Ismail
rulers.note: Reigned 1863-1879; the khedive title came by firman in 1867. Only the years to 1865 belong to this dossier.

correction.text: Egypt as Cliopatria draws it for Muhammad Ali from 1811: the Nile valley, the Delta, Sinai and the Red Sea coast

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1805-1810 shape is 6 cells (1,771 km2) around Cairo, which is Muhammad Ali's seat and nothing like his province: 'in 1805 he was named Wāli (governor) of Egypt and gained the rank of Pasha' (infobox term from 17 May 1805) and the Sultan acknowledged his position. Use the Egypt of the 1811 shape for 1805-1810. The Mamluks held Upper Egypt in this period on the usual account; the pages opened do not give the extent of their rule (page budget), so Upper Egypt is not removed.

correction.text: unchanged shape, drawn for 1811-1819: Egypt only

keyframe_review.note: 604,573 km2 for 1811-1821: Egypt without the Hejaz or Sudan. Years only: the shape holds for 1811-1819. The Ottoman-Egyptian army fought the Emirate of Diriyah for the Hejaz and Najd from early 1811 (Tusun Pasha landed at Yanbu) to 1818, but the land passed to the Ottoman Empire and is not Muhammad Ali's until the Convention of Kutahya (1833), as Cliopatria draws it.

correction.text: Egypt and Nubia, which 'at once submitted' in July 1820

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Ismail left Cairo in July 1820 to conquer the Sudan and 'Nubia at once submitted'; Cliopatria adds the Sudan only in 1822.

correction.text: the 1822 shape (Egypt, Nubia, Sennar, Kordofan, the Khartoum region) drawn one year early, for 1821

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Ali's troops made headway into Sudan in 1821'; Sennar 'was reduced without a battle' and Kordofan fell after a hard-fought engagement (History of Egypt page). The 1822 shape applies from 1821. The ledger now splits the conquest: Sennar and the Gezira from the Funj on 14 June 1821 (Sultanate of Sennar page) and Kordofan from Darfur on 19 August 1821 (Sultanate of Darfur page; the Sennar page says the Fur Sultanate held Kordofan until the Egyptian invasion of 1821).

1,643,446 km2 for 1822-1833: Egypt with Nubia, Sennar, Kordofan and the Khartoum region. The page lists the 'Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan (1820-1824)'; the Darfur lands (1 percent of Darfur) are not in the shape: 'Eventually, Egypt successfully annexed the region of Darfur', undated. Area check: the History of Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty page (the Cliopatria title) has no infobox and no km2 figure (re-checked 2026-10-25), and the Muhammad Ali of Egypt infobox has none either, so no ratio can be computed for this shape. Darfur: the Turco-Egyptian Sudan page gives 1874 as the only dated annexation of Darfur (outside this dossier). Crete is governed from 1821 (ledger occupation, hatched) but drawn as territory only from 1833.

correction.text: Egypt, the Sudan, Syria, Cilicia, the Hejaz, Crete and the Tihama coast, as granted at Kutahya and taken in 1833

keyframe_review.note: 2,313,597 km2 for 1834-1839, drawn here for 1834-1838 (1839 has its own keyframe): Egypt, the Sudan, Syria, Adana, and the Hejaz. The Convention of Kutahya (May 1833) left Ibrahim Pasha governor of the Syrian provinces ('Ottoman cession of Syria to Egypt', infobox) and gave the Hejaz and Crete (Muhammad Ali page). Crete (27 cells) and the Tihama coast, which the Yemen Eyalet page has taken from the ruler in Sana'a by the 'Ottoman viceroy of Egypt in 1833', are not in Cliopatria's shape and are added here; the Hejaz is the page's. 'From the Sudan to the Taurus Mountains' (History of Egypt page, 1833). The Syrian provinces, Crete and the Hejaz are the Sultan's vassal land (ottoman-empire /ledger/181).

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state (Emirate of Jabal Shammar page)

correction.text: the 1834 shape with Crete, the Tihama coast, Najd and al-Hasa (without the Ha'il province), after Faisal's defeat in 1838

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Emirate of Nejd page has Faisal 'defeated and taken to Ottoman Egypt as a prisoner for the second time in 1838' after a re-invasion organised by Muhammad Ali, and the Ottomans installing Khalid bin Saud with Ottoman-Egyptian troops; Cliopatria adds Najd to the Egyptian shape only in 1840. The page gives no Egyptian garrison or boundary (Najd as a region, held through the client). Fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): now Najd and al-Hasa without the Ha'il province. Expedition to Najd (1836) page: "Mehmet Ali had occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif" (Faisal defeated by Hurshid Pasha in 1838); the page does not say that Egypt occupied Ha'il or mention the Rashidis. Emirate of Jabal Shammar page: "The Emirate of Jabal Shammar was established in 1836 as a vassal of the second Saudi state" (infobox "Nominal vassal of the Second Saudi State (1836-1848)"), with no word of the Egyptians. The gazetteer's Najd (2,180 cells) had included Ha'il (453 cells), which emirate-of-jabal-shammar holds from 1836. Hasa moves here from 1840 (/ledger/20). The keyframe is the end-of-1839 land.

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state (Emirate of Jabal Shammar page)

correction.text: the end-of-1840 land: Egypt, the Sinai and the Sudan with Najd and al-Hasa (without the Ha'il province)

keyframe_review.note: 2,689,225 km2, the maximum: Syria, the Hejaz and (in Cliopatria) Najd and Hasa. Years only: the shape holds for 1840 until the autumn, when Beirut was abandoned (3 October), Acre taken (3-4 November) and the Convention of Alexandria accepted (27 November 1840); Crete and the Tihama are added. Najd (about 1,050 cells) is dated 1838 by the Emirate of Nejd page (Faisal defeated and taken to Egypt) and drawn from 1839; Hasa (about 210 cells) is on no page (the Nejd page is silent on it). Fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): the keyframe is now the end-of-1840 land. The ledger already takes Syria and Adana, Crete, the Hejaz and the Tihama away in November 1840 (/ledger/22-25; Egyptian-Ottoman War (1839-1841) page: the Egyptians "had abandoned Beirut on October 3", Acre occupied on 3-4 November, "Muhammad Ali finally accepted the terms of the Convention on 27 November 1840", he "withdrew from Syria, the Hijaz, the Holy Land, Adana and Crete"), and the compiler sets a keyframe against the state after the year's events, so the earlier maximum-extent shape was snapped against its own ledger (13,974 cells before the snap, 9,858 in the keyframe, 4,261 removed, 164 added). Najd and al-Hasa stay ("The rule over Najd ended by the close of 1841", Expedition to Najd (1836) page), taken as the page's named regions in place of Cliopatria's partial share (1,053 and 212 cells), without the Ha'il province (24 cells of Cliopatria's shape). Egypt, the Sinai and the Sudan are Cliopatria's 1842 shape, identical to the 1840 shape in Egypt and the Sudan.

correction.text: Egypt, the Sinai and the Sudan at the end of 1841

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps Syria and the Hejaz for 1841 although the pages end the Egyptian hold on them on 27 November 1840: Muhammad Ali 'finally accepted the terms of the Convention' and gave up Syria, the Holy Land, Crete, Adana and the Hejaz. 1841 is the 1842 shape plus the Najd and Hasa land that Cliopatria still shows (unverified). Fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): the keyframe is now the end-of-1841 land. /ledger/26 ends the Egyptian hold on Najd and al-Hasa in 1841 (Expedition to Najd (1836) page: "The rule over Najd ended by the close of 1841"), so the year's land is the 1842 shape; the former keyframe drew Cliopatria's Najd and Hasa share back after that loss (875 cells added at the snap, 1,524 kept by the Emirate of Nejd) and carried 24 cells of the Ha'il province.

1,648,472 km2 for 1842-1847: Egypt, the Sinai and the Sudan, as the firman of 13 February 1841 confined the pasha's authority to Egypt, 'the Sinai peninsula and certain places on the Arabian side of the Red Sea, and to the Sudan'; the Arabian places are not in the shape.

1,834,672 km2 for 1848-1864: the Sudan share grows by about 580 cells and Upper Egypt by a few. No page dates the growth (the Turco-Egyptian Sudan page, opened after review, is silent on 1848, dates Kassala and Taka to 1840 and the Red Sea coast cession to 1865, and gives no date for Upper Nile, Bahr al Ghazal and Equatoria); the History of Egypt page says only that control of 'the Red Sea ports of Suakin and Massawa' came 'in the following years' after Khartoum was founded, and is silent on an 1865 lease.

1865, the last year of the Cliopatria row; the same land continues as the Khedivate of Egypt (khedive title by firman of 1867; the page mentions a firman of 1866). Area check: the Khedivate of Egypt infobox gives 5,000,000 km2 (a footnote says inhabited areas only; no year given) against 1,834,672 km2 here, ratio 0.37; with no year and a different definition the figure is not a verdict on the shape.

region.text: Egypt as Cliopatria draws it for Muhammad Ali from 1811: the Nile valley, the Delta, Sinai and the Red Sea coast

ledger.note: 1805: Muhammad Ali becomes wali of Egypt. His term runs from 17 May 1805 (infobox); 'in 1805 he was named Wāli (governor) of Egypt and gained the rank of Pasha' after a group of Egyptians 'demanded the replacement of Wāli (governor) Hurshid Pasha by Muhammad Ali, and the Ottomans yielded'. The page names Egypt, not a boundary.

region.text: Egypt as the pasha held it from 1805, and then whatever land the keyframes give the dynasty: a vassal of the Sultan throughout

ledger.note: 1805: Muhammad Ali's Egypt is the Sultan's vassal from the start. The page: Muhammad Ali Pasha 'taking control of Egypt in 1805, when the Ottoman Sultan acknowledged his position'; in 1833 he rules 'a virtually independent empire... subject only to a moderate annual tribute', and the firman of 13 February 1841 laid restrictions on him 'emphasizing his position as vassal'. The Muhammad Ali of Egypt page calls him an 'Ottoman viceroy and governor' (term from 17 May 1805, infobox). Mirror of ottoman-empire /ledger/159 (vassal_start 1805). The relation covers whatever land the keyframes give the dynasty; the Syrian provinces, Crete and the Hejaz of 1833-1840 are the same vassalage and are written here as a gain and losses from ottoman-empire (the Ottoman side has them as vassal_start 1833-5 and vassal_end 1840-11, /ledger/181 and /ledger/185); see notes. Added after review (the first draft had no vassal event).

region.text: the Hejaz, where the landing and the fighting of 1811-1815 were

ledger.note: 1811: the Ottoman-Egyptian army lands in Arabia against the Emirate of Diriyah. Muhammad Ali's troops 'landed in Yanbu under the command of his son Tusun Pasha' (Wahhabi War); Medina fell in late 1812, Jeddah a month later and Mecca in January 1813, both 'without a fight', and the war lasted 'from early 1811 until 1818'. Narrowed in fx-52 (K01) from the Hejaz and Najd together: the Wahhabi War page dates no fighting in Najd before 1816 ('the Ottomans resumed the war in 1816', and only then did Ibrahim Pasha advance into Central Arabia), so the Najd contest is opened in 1816 (below), as in ottoman-empire /ledger/170. The Hejaz contest closes with the treaty of spring 1815 (below).

region.text: the Hejaz

ledger.note: Spring 1815: 'In the spring of 1815, Ottoman forces inflicted large-scale defeat upon the Saudis, forcing them to conclude a peace treaty'; the Wahhabis had to give up the Hijaz and Abdullah ibn Saud was to acknowledge himself a vassal (Wahhabi War; the page adds that 'Neither Muhammad Ali nor the Ottoman Sultan had confirmed the treaty'). Mirrors ottoman-empire /ledger/169 and emirate-of-diriyah /ledger/25. A contest_end closes the whole relation of the pair, so the Najd contest of 1816 is opened afresh. Added in fx-52 (K01).

region.text: Najd, from Al-Qassim to Diriyah

ledger.note: 1816: the Ottomans 'resumed the war in 1816', with Ibrahim Pasha leading the advance into Central Arabia; by 1817 'their forces had overrun Rass, Buraida, and Unayza', Ibrahim's forces reached the capital by April 1818 and the siege of Diriyah ended with the surrender of 11 September 1818 (Wahhabi War). Mirrors ottoman-empire /ledger/170 and emirate-of-diriyah /ledger/26. Added in fx-52 (K01): the Najd part of the contest used to open in 1811 with the Hejaz, though the page places no fighting in Najd before 1816. The ledger/5 contest_end of September 1818 closes this relation.

region.text: the Hejaz and Najd

ledger.note: 1818: Diriyah falls to Ibrahim Pasha. His forces arrived by April 1818 and the siege lasted until September; on 11 September 1818 Abdullah ibn Saud offered his surrender, and the city was razed. Ibrahim returned to Egypt in December 1819 'after formally incorporating Hejaz into the Ottoman Empire'; the Egyptian garrison in Najd is not on the page.

region.text: Nubia, which 'at once submitted'

ledger.note: 1820: Muhammad Ali's army enters the Sudan. Ismail left Cairo in July 1820; 'Nubia at once submitted'. Counterpart nobody (reviewer fix): the Muhammad Ali of Egypt page says the Sultanate of Sennar had declined and its former territories had broken into rival kingdoms, the Shaigiya resisting; the funj-sultanate dossier confines the Funj to the Gezira from 1802.

region.text: Crete, 'occupied with a small Egyptian force'

ledger.note: 1821: Muhammad Ali is made governor of Crete. The page: 'Mehemet Ali had already, in 1821, been appointed by him governor of Crete, which he had occupied with a small Egyptian force' (the Sultan's appointment, in the Greek War of Independence). The page does not date the occupation and says nothing of Egyptian rule between 1821 and 1840; the Muhammad Ali of Egypt page adds only that the Sultan 'offered Muhammad Ali the island of Crete in exchange for his support in putting down the revolt' (undated). 1821 is the year of the appointment, so the start is a bridge (confidence 1). Counterpart ottoman-empire is the island's sovereign, for whom the force held it; the occupation ends when the Convention of Kutahya grants the island (May 1833). Cliopatria and the keyframes draw Crete Ottoman until 1833. Added after review (the first notes said no page dates Egyptian rule of Crete).

region.text: Sennar and the Gezira

ledger.note: 14 June 1821: Sennar falls. The Sultanate of Sennar page: 'On 14 June they received the official submission of Badi VII', the last Funj sultan, who 'surrendered to the Turco-Egyptian conquest without resistance'; the Turks reached the Nile confluence in May 1821 and found Sennar 'now reduced to a heap of ruins'. The page names Sennar, not the Gezira, but says 'After 1802, the authority of the sultanate was limited to the Gezira for good' (funj-sultanate /ledger/20 loses 'Sennar and the Gezira' in June 1821, so the region is the Funj dossier's reading). The History of Egypt page: Sennar 'was reduced without a battle'. Half of the former /ledger/4 (split after review: Kordofan was Darfur's).

region.text: Kordofan

ledger.note: 19 August 1821: Kordofan falls. The Sultanate of Darfur page: 'The Keira dispatched another army but it was routed by the Egyptians near Bara on 19 August 1821', and 'In 1821, the Turco-Egyptians under Muhammad Ali ... conquered the Funj and the province of Kordofan'. The Sultanate of Sennar page: 'the Fur Sultanate conquered Kordofan which it managed to hold until the Egyptian invasion of 1821', so Kordofan was Darfur's, not the Funj's; sultanate-of-darfur /ledger/6 records the same loss on 19 August 1821. The History of Egypt page: Mahommed Bey's force took Kordofan 'not without a hard-fought engagement' (no date). The other half of the former /ledger/4, which named funj-sultanate.

region.text: the Morea, where Ibrahim landed (the page names no towns)

ledger.note: March 1825: Ibrahim lands in the Morea. A fleet of 60 Egyptian warships carried troops to Suda Bay in the autumn of 1824, and the army 'in the following March, with Ibrahin as commander-in-chief landed in the Morea' (the page does not write the year; it follows from the autumn of 1824). Egypt fought for the Sultan, so the land stays Ottoman in law and the Egyptian army holds it: an occupation, not a gain. The page does not say which places Ibrahim held, so the whole Peloponnese is named (ottoman-empire /ledger/170 contests it with the Greeks from 1821). Added after review.

region.text: the Morea, where Ibrahim landed (the page names no towns)

ledger.note: August 1828: Egypt agrees to recall Ibrahim. The page: 'the withdrawal of the Egyptians from the Morea was ultimately due to the action of Admiral Sir Edward Codrington, who early in August 1828 appeared before Alexandria'; his threat of bombardment led the pasha to sign a convention to recall Ibrahim and his army. The page gives no signing day and no date for the last Egyptian troops leaving; the Muhammad Ali of Egypt page has the Egyptians 'forced to withdraw' after Navarino (20 October 1827), undated. Added after review.

region.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

ledger.note: 1831: Ibrahim Pasha invades Syria. The infobox dates the First Egyptian-Ottoman War 10 October 1831 - 8 April 1833; land and sea forces were sent to besiege Acre 'in October 1831'.

region.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

ledger.note: 1832: Acre falls and Syria is occupied. Acre 'fell six months later in May 1832' (27 May 1832 in the Muhammad Ali of Egypt page, after a siege from 3 November 1831); Ibrahim then took control of Damascus, Aleppo, Homs, Beirut, Sidon and Tripoli on dates the page does not give. Konya was won on 21 December 1832.

region.text: the coast wrested from the ruler in Sana'a

ledger.note: 1833: Egypt takes the Tihama. The Yemen Eyalet page: 'new intervention by the Ottoman viceroy of Egypt in 1833 again wrested the coast from the ruler in Sana'a'. The page does not name Muhammad Ali (he is the Ottoman viceroy of Egypt of these years), names no towns and gives no month; 'the coast' is read as the Tihama, as in the imamate-of-yemen dossier, which records the loss in its /ledger/2. Cliopatria's Egyptian shapes never held the coast; the 1834 and 1840 keyframes add it. Added after review (mirror of imamate-of-yemen /ledger/2).

region.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

ledger.note: 1833: the Convention of Kutahya turns the occupation of Syria into a cession (May 1833; the page gives no day, the Muhammad Ali dynasty page 14 May, the war infobox ends 8 April 1833).

region.text: Crete, 'occupied with a small Egyptian force'

ledger.note: May 1833: the occupation of Crete becomes a grant. Under the Convention of Kutahya Muhammad Ali was to 'receive the territories of Crete (then known as Candia) and the Hijaz as compensation' (page; no day given). Closes the 1821 occupation of the island.

region.text: the Syrian provinces, Cilicia, Crete and the Hejaz

ledger.note: 1833: the Ottomans cede Syria to Egypt. Infobox 'Ottoman cession of Syria to Egypt'; Ibrahim Pasha 'would be appointed Wāli of Syria' and Muhammad Ali was to receive 'the territories of Crete' and 'the Hijaz' as compensation (Muhammad Ali of Egypt page); the Muhammad Ali dynasty page lists 'the pashaliks of Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli'.

region.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

ledger.note: 1833: the First Egyptian-Ottoman War ends with the Convention of Kutahya after Russian intervention ('Egyptian victory').

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state (Emirate of Jabal Shammar page)

region.text: Najd without the Ha'il province

ledger.note: 1838: Faisal bin Turki is defeated and Najd comes under Egyptian arms. The Emirate of Nejd page: Faisal 'faced a re-invasion of Najd organised by Muhammad Ali' and 'was defeated and taken to Ottoman Egypt as a prisoner for the second time in 1838'; 'The Ottomans installed Khalid bin Saud', backed by Ottoman-Egyptian troops (no date). The page is silent on Egyptian garrisons and does not mention Hofuf; the Muhammad Ali of Egypt infobox lists an 'Expedition to Najd (1836)'. Najd is held through the client Khalid, hence confidence 2. Cliopatria adds Najd to the Egyptian shape only in 1840. Moved from 1840 and narrowed to Najd after review (the thin note on the former /ledger/11). Fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): the region leaves out the Ha'il province. Expedition to Najd (1836) page: Muhammad Ali's forces landed at Yanbu in 1836, Khalid entered Riyadh in 1837, Hurshid Pasha defeated Faisal in 1838 and "Mehmet Ali had occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif"; the page does not say Egypt took Ha'il. Emirate of Jabal Shammar page: Ha'il "established in 1836 as a vassal of the second Saudi state", no word of the Egyptians.

region.text: Hasa

ledger.note: 1838: al-Hasa comes under Egyptian arms with Najd. Expedition to Najd (1836) page (read 2026-11-01): "Mehmet Ali had occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif" in the campaign that ended with Hurshid Pasha's defeat of Faisal in 1838; the page dates al-Hasa separately nowhere, so the year of the Najd gain (/ledger/19) is used (bridge, confidence 1). The former /ledger/19 dated this gain to 1840, the year Cliopatria adds Hasa (about 210 cells) to its Egyptian shape, but the same page has most of the army recalled from Najd and eastern Arabia in April 1840. The region is the gazetteer's Hasa (the Eastern Province), as the Emirate of Nejd dossier draws it. Moved from 1840 by fix fx-16.

region.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

ledger.note: 1839: the second Egyptian-Ottoman War. On 24 June 1839 an Ottoman army 'was destroyed in Syria by Muhammad Ali's general Ibrahim Pasha' at Nezib, and on 1 July the Ottoman fleet 'sailed to Alexandria and surrendered to Muhammad Ali'.

region.text: Syria, the Holy Land and Adana

ledger.note: 1840: the Egyptians lose Syria. Napier bombarded Beirut on 11 September 1840 ('open war broke out'), the Egyptians 'abandoned Beirut' on 3 October, Sidon capitulated and Acre was occupied on the night of 3-4 November; on 27 November Muhammad Ali accepted the terms and gave up Syria, the Holy Land and Adana.

region.text: Crete and the Hejaz

ledger.note: 1840: Muhammad Ali renounces Crete and the Hejaz in the Convention of Alexandria (27 November 1840): 'Egyptian retrocession of Syria, Crete, and the Hejaz to the Ottoman Empire'; the page gives no end date for Egyptian control of the Hejaz itself.

region.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

ledger.note: 1840: the war ends on 27 November 1840, when Muhammad Ali 'finally accepted the terms of the Convention' (the Convention of Alexandria); an Ottoman victory, with hereditary rule of Egypt and the Sudan kept and an army of 18,000 men.

region.text: the coast wrested from the ruler in Sana'a

ledger.note: 27 November 1840 (Convention of Alexandria): the end of the Egyptian hold on the Tihama is bridged. The Yemen Eyalet page is silent on an Egyptian withdrawal and on who held the coast afterwards; it says the Ottomans 'returned to the Tihama in 1849 after an absence of two centuries'. The Muhammad Ali of Egypt page names only Crete and the Hejaz among the lands renounced; the History of Egypt page leaves the pasha, by the firman of 13 February 1841, 'certain places on the Arabian side of the Red Sea' (unnamed); the Emirate of Nejd page says the Ottoman Empire 'withdrew their military presence in the Arabian Peninsula' after the 1840 Convention. Counterpart nobody for want of a page naming the next holder; imamate-of-yemen draws no Tihama until 1872. Added after review.

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state (Emirate of Jabal Shammar page)

region.text: Najd and Hasa without the Ha'il province

ledger.note: 1841: the Egyptian hold on Najd and Hasa ends. Expedition to Najd (1836) page (read 2026-11-01): "European pressure and British diplomacy led to the recall of most of the army from Najd and eastern Arabia in April 1840" and "The rule over Najd ended by the close of 1841"; Faisal escaped from Cairo in 1843 and began a second reign. The page gives no month for the end of the rule and says nothing of al-Hasa after 1840, so al-Hasa goes with Najd (bridge). Emirate of Nejd page (read 2026-10-25): after the 1840 Convention of London "the Ottoman Empire withdrew their military presence in the Arabian Peninsula". Counterpart emirate-of-nejd as the next holder is the pages' reading. Revised by fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): source and confidence 1 to 2, the Ha'il province left out, and the 1841 keyframe no longer draws the land back.

region.text: Egypt as the pasha held it from 1805, and then whatever land the keyframes give the dynasty: a vassal of the Sultan throughout

ledger.note: 1865: bookkeeping end of this dossier's vassal span, not an end of the relation. The Muhammad Ali dynasty goes on as the Sultan's vassal in the Khedivate of Egypt ('an autonomous tributary state of the Ottoman Empire', Khedivate of Egypt page, title by firman of 8 June 1867); the relation passes to khedivate-of-egypt, whose dossier should open its own. The Ottoman side records the dynasty's relation to 1865 (ottoman-empire /ledger/190); khedivate-of-egypt /ledger/1 and /ledger/27 carry the vassalage from 1866 to December 1914 (the former ottoman-empire /ledger/225, a 1914 end under this slug, was dropped in fx-52, K03). Added after review.

region.text: Egypt and the Sudan, passed to the Khedivate of Egypt

ledger.note: 1865: the pasha's Egypt continues as the Khedivate. The page mentions a firman in 1866 and the khedive title by firman in 1867; Cliopatria ends this row in 1865 and starts the Khedivate of Egypt in 1866 (bridging at confidence 1). Second page, Khedivate of Egypt: the infobox gives 'Established: 8 June 1867' (the title 'declared by a firman on 8 June 1867'); the page is silent on a firman of 1866, so the 1865 year stays Cliopatria's bridge (confidence 1).

wars.name: Ottoman-Wahhabi War
wars.outcome: Destruction of the Emirate of Diriyah; the Hejaz returned to Ottoman rule, with Egyptian armies as the Sultan's agent.
wars.note: Fought for the Sultan by Muhammad Ali's sons Tusun and Ibrahim; the page names the belligerents as the Ottoman Empire, its vassal the Eyalet of Egypt, and the Emirate of Diriyah. A treaty of spring 1815 giving up the Hejaz was never confirmed. Page budget: the Diriyah dossier has the fuller chronology.

wars.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
wars.outcome: Egypt takes Nubia (July 1820), Sennar and the Gezira from the Funj (14 June 1821) and Kordofan from Darfur (19 August 1821) and builds the Sudan province.
wars.note: The Muhammad Ali of Egypt page lists the 'Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan (1820-1824)' and gives only 1820 (an army of 5,000) and 1821. The Sultanate of Sennar and Sultanate of Darfur pages (opened after review) date Sennar and Kordofan; the History of Egypt page gives neither Kordofan's date nor Darfur.

wars.name: Egyptian intervention in the Greek War of Independence

zones.text: the Morea, where Ibrahim landed in March 1825, and Crete, whose governorship Muhammad Ali held from 1821

wars.outcome: No border change: Egypt held land for the Sultan and kept none. Ibrahim's army occupied (parts of) the Morea from March 1825 to the convention of early August 1828, which recalled it after Codrington's threat (the Battle of Navarino was on 20 October 1827); Crete, governed by Muhammad Ali from 1821, stayed Ottoman until it was granted to him at Kutahya in 1833.
wars.note: A fleet of 60 Egyptian warships carried troops to Suda Bay in the autumn of 1824; Ibrahim landed in the Morea 'in the following March' (1825); Admiral Codrington appeared before Alexandria in early August 1828 (History of Egypt page). Muhammad Ali had 'already, in 1821, been appointed ... governor of Crete, which he had occupied with a small Egyptian force' (same page, undated occupation); the Muhammad Ali of Egypt page says the Sultan offered him Crete for his support (undated). Ledger: occupation of the Morea 1825-1828 and of Crete 1821-1833.

wars.name: Egyptian-Ottoman War (1831-1833)

zones.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: the Ottomans cede Syria to Egypt by the Convention of Kutahya (May 1833).
wars.note: Infobox 10 October 1831 - 8 April 1833; Acre fell in May 1832 and Konya on 21 December 1832.

wars.name: Egyptian-Ottoman War (1839-1841)

zones.text: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo and Itcheli (Cilicia): the pashaliks the Convention of Kutahya granted

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory with British naval support: Egypt gives up Syria, Crete, Adana and the Hejaz and keeps hereditary rule of Egypt and the Sudan (27 November 1840; firman of 13 February 1841).
wars.note: Nezib 24 June 1839; Napier before Beirut on 11 August 1840; Beirut abandoned 3 October and Acre taken 3-4 November 1840.

certainty.note: Egypt's own edge is the desert; the Hejaz, Sudan and Syrian lines were army zones, not surveyed frontiers.

The firman of 13 February 1841 names the extent in words (Egypt, 'the Sinai peninsula and certain places on the Arabian side of the Red Sea, and to the Sudan'); no survey line, and the Sudan's southern and western limits stay open.

notes:
Cliopatria: the 1805-1810 shape (6 cells at Cairo) is wrong and is replaced by the Egypt of the 1811 shape; the ottoman-empire dossier draws Egypt inside its own shape to 1810 and records the vassalage from 1805 (ottoman-empire /ledger/159, mirrored here by the vassal_start of May 1805), so the two overlap and the renderer must choose the lighter tint. Vassalage (repair): the vassal span runs through the whole dossier, 1805-1865, and passes to khedivate-of-egypt (the vassal_end of 1865 is bookkeeping for the dissolve). The Ottoman dossier also records the Syrian provinces, Crete and the Hejaz of 1833-1840 as a vassal_start 1833-5 and vassal_end 1840-11 naming this state (ottoman-empire /ledger/181 and /ledger/185); this dossier writes the same grant as a gain from ottoman-empire in May 1833 and the losses of November 1840 and opens no second vassal pair, because two open spans with one counterpart string cannot be told apart; the Egyptian pasha was the Sultan's vassal for all that land, as the History of Egypt page says of the settlement of 1841 ('emphasizing his position as vassal'). The Ottoman side records the dynasty's relation to 1865 (ottoman-empire /ledger/190); khedivate-of-egypt /ledger/1 and /ledger/27 carry the vassalage from 1866 to December 1914 (the former ottoman-empire /ledger/225, a 1914 end under this slug, was dropped in fx-52, K03). Hejaz and Najd 1811-1833 (corrected after review): ottoman-empire takes them from the Emirate of Diriyah (/ledger/163 Hejaz 1812, /ledger/169 Najd 1818, the Egyptian army as the Sultan's agent), whereas emirate-of-diriyah records its losses of 1811-1818 (/ledger/18-23 and /ledger/26) and its dissolve (/ledger/29) to muhammad-ali-dynasty. This dossier records the war as a contest only and the Hejaz as Egyptian from the Convention of Kutahya (1833), as Cliopatria does; the three dossiers disagree on who holds the land between 1812 and 1833 and the orchestrator should choose one holder. Crete (corrected after review): the History of Egypt page does date it: Muhammad Ali was 'already, in 1821, ... appointed ... governor of Crete, which he had occupied with a small Egyptian force'. The page is silent on the occupation date and on Egyptian rule between 1821 and 1840, so the ledger holds an occupation_start of 1821 at confidence 1, closed by the grant of the island at Kutahya (May 1833); Crete is drawn as territory from 1834. Greek war (repair): Ibrahim's army in the Morea, March 1825 to the convention of early August 1828, is an occupation (counterpart first-hellenic-republic); the page names no towns, so the whole Peloponnese is the region. Sudan (repair): the old Kordofan-from-Funj gain is split into Sennar and the Gezira from the Funj (14 June 1821, Sultanate of Sennar page) and Kordofan from Darfur (19 August 1821, Sultanate of Darfur page). The turco-egyptian-sudan dossier (another batch) treats the Sudan as a state from July 1820 with this state as the founding counterpart and has the same Sennar date; this dossier keeps the Sudan inside the dynasty's shapes, as Cliopatria does, so the overlap is intended. Tihama (repair): the 1833 gain from imamate-of-yemen mirrors imamate-of-yemen /ledger/2 (Yemen Eyalet page). The end of the Egyptian hold is undated on every page opened (the Ottomans 'returned to the Tihama in 1849'), so the loss stands at the Convention of Alexandria (November 1840) at confidence 1, with counterpart nobody. Najd and Hasa (repair): the Emirate of Nejd page dates Faisal's defeat and removal to Egypt to 1838, so Najd is a gain of 1838 (drawn from 1839, confidence 2) instead of 1840; it is silent on Hasa (kept at 1840, confidence 1) and dates the end only as 'following the 1840 Convention of London', so the loss of both stands at 1841, confidence 1. Area: the History of Egypt page has no infobox and no km2 figure (re-checked 2026-10-25); no Cliopatria shape of this row can be compared with a page figure. The Khedivate of Egypt infobox gives 5,000,000 km2 (inhabited areas only, undated) against 1,834,672 km2 in 1865. Not settled: the Mamluk beys of Upper Egypt (extent and date driven out are on no page opened; they need a dossier, counterpart 'Mamluk beys of Egypt', group me-10-x); the Sudan's growth after 1841 (the Turco-Egyptian Sudan page is silent on 1848; Suakin and Massawa undated); the 1865 dissolve (Cliopatria's bridge to its Khedivate row of 1866; the Khedivate page says 8 June 1867 and is silent on a firman of 1866, while the History page has a firman of 1866 on tribute and succession); the date of the Convention of Kutahya (5 May on the Ottoman dossier's page, 14 May on the History page, 'May 1833' on Muhammad Ali's page, none on the war page whose infobox ends 8 April 1833); Ibrahim's conquest of Qatif and al-Hasa (Wahhabi War page, undated). The page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Saudi_War does not exist (url_not_found); the article is Wahhabi War. The dynasty itself ran to 1953 (History of Egypt page); the dossier ends in 1865 where Cliopatria's Khedivate of Egypt begins in 1866.
Fix fx-16 (2026-11-01), snap of 1840 and the Ha'il overlap: the 1839 keyframe and the Hasa gain used the gazetteer's Najd (2,180 cells, 453 of them the Ha'il province that emirate-of-jabal-shammar holds from 1836) and Hasa (the whole Eastern Province, 2,447 cells) while the 1840 and 1841 keyframes used Cliopatria's partial share (1,053 and 212 cells), and the 1840 keyframe kept Syria, the Hejaz, Crete and the Tihama that the ledger takes away in November 1840. The keyframes of 1839, 1840 and 1841 are now the end-of-year land, built from the regions the Expedition to Najd (1836) page names, without Ha'il; the Hasa gain moved from 1840 to 1838 (/ledger/20). About 1,350 of the 4,261 cells removed at the 1840 snap are whole admin1 units (Al Hudud ash Shamaliyah 454, Najran 365, Al Jawf 331, Dhofar 66) that match in place and size (Najran 365 of 378, Al Jawf 331 of 417, Dhofar 66, Northern Borders 454 of 469) the lands of emirate-of-diriyah's 1815 loss (/23, the south and east of the 1814 shape) and 1818 dissolve (/29, the 1815 shape), which name this dynasty as counterpart; unverified, the Diriyah pages were not opened in this run; they are not in any region of this dossier (see the handoff in the fx-16 report).
